[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "paddock (Middle English paddok) = toad/frog; from Old English *pad, *padda + -oc diminutive; also paddock = enclosure, from Old English pearroc",
    "reading": "A small enclosed field, or a diminutive toad — the land's humble guardian and the amphibian's hidden threshold.",
    "languages": ["en", "ang"],
    "source": "OED, s.v. paddock n.1 and n.2",
    "confidence": 0.9
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "pad + dock; pad (soft cushion, footstep) + dock (water plant, or ship's berth, or cut short)",
    "reading": "Soft footfall at the water's edge — a place where the boat is moored and the leaf is cut.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "paddock ~ French 'patte d'eau' (paw of water) ~ 'patois' (dialect) ~ 'paddock' in French = field (from English)",
    "reading": "A water-paw, a dialect of the land — the field speaks in wet footprints.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "paddock → 'pad dock' → 'dock pad' → 'dap dock' (dap = to bounce, to fish with a fly)",
    "reading": "The dock's bounce — a leaping place where the fish rises to the fly, a hidden spring.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "P-A-D-D-O-C-K → Pater Aeternus, Deus, Dominus, Omnium, Creator, Keeper (Latin initials)",
    "reading": "Eternal Father, God, Lord of all, Creator, Keeper — the field as a sacred enclosure.",
    "languages": ["la", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "P (Greek rho, breath) + A (alpha, beginning) + D (delta, door) + D (door) + O (omega, end) + C (kappa, hand) + K (kaph, palm)",
    "reading": "Breath through the beginning and double door to the end — the hand that holds the palm.",
    "languages": ["grc", "he", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "P=80, A=1, D=4, D=4, O=15, C=3, K=11 (Greek isopsephy) → 80+1+4+4+15+3+11 = 118; 1+1+8=10 → 1",
    "reading": "Sum 118 reduces to 1 — the monad, the enclosure as the first unity, the singular field.",
    "languages": ["grc", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "paddock (enclosure) from Old English pearroc, from Proto-Germanic *parrukaz, from Latin *parricus (fence); related to 'park'",
    "reading": "A fenced park, a bounded paradise — the word carries the memory of the original garden.",
    "languages": ["en", "la", "gem"],
    "source": "OED, s.v. park; Pokorny, IEW",
    "confidence": 0.85
  }
]
